metadata.title: Cerebras: Wafer-Scale Chips, Skipping HBM, and a Near-$100B IPO
metadata.guest_role: Cerebras CEO and early backers (SV101 documentary)

conclusion: SV101 traces Cerebras from a 2015 whiteboard to a May 2026 IPO that printed $55.5B raised, $311 first-day close (+68%), and a peak near $100B. The bet was a wafer-scale engine — 58× a top GPU — that skips HBM, CoWoS, and TSMC 3nm, the three scarcest AI-chip bottlenecks. Baidu's early scaling-law work (300M-param LM, later carried to OpenAI by Dario) created the demand; G42's $1B+ Condor Galaxy both scaled the company and almost killed the first listing. Inference cloud now claims >2000 tok/s versus 200–300, and Feldman will partner every hyperscaler except NVIDIA.
background: Documentary-style episode with early investor Zhou Nan, ex-NVIDIA/Baidu researcher Greg Diamos, and product execs. Arc: SeaMicro five leave AMD after the $334M sale, hide for three years at ~$8M/month burn, ship WSE-1 in 2019, live on DOE labs, then G42, OpenAI, AWS, and the IPO.
important_facts: 2014–15 origin: Baidu Silicon Valley lab ($300M) trains a then-largest 300M-param LM in three months and writes the empirical scaling-law paper Dario later takes to OpenAI. Same year five SeaMicro/AMD engineers (Feldman, Lauterbach, James, Lie, Fricker) decide one wafer should be the chip — area ~58× the largest GPU, on-die SRAM instead of HBM hops. Yield trick: 1–1.5% spare cores plus on-chip fabric, scaled from H100's 144/132 spare-core idea to a whole wafer. 2016–mid-2019 stealth: ~$8M/month burn, ~$300M over three years, 25kW on a dinner-plate, first customers 'maybe a dozen' CS-1s.

Proof then scale: WSE-1 at Hot Chips 2019 (45k+ mm², 400k cores, 18GB on-die SRAM vs tens of MB on peer GPUs); $272M E round. DOE labs (Argonne COVID, Livermore fusion, NETL ~500× vs their supercomputer). WSE-2 (2021, 7nm, 850k cores, 2.6T transistors); CS-2 trains a 20B model on one box (2022); CHM exhibit. Series F Nov 2021 at $4B. G42 Condor Galaxy 2023: >$1B, 4 exaflops, a 6.5-ft box built in 10 days — also the customer that blew up the first IPO attempt. Gen-3 sales 'in the tens of thousands' after gen-1 teens and gen-2 ~300.

2024–26 product stack: chip → CS system → Andromeda (16× CS-2, 13.5M cores, >1 exaflop, 500kW) → Cerebras Inference (Aug 2024, OpenAI-API compatible, >2000 tok/s vs 200–300). Mar 2026 AWS: others do prefill, Cerebras does serial decode — every hyperscaler except NVIDIA. S-1 refiled Apr 17, 2026; lists May 14; IPO range $120–160, prints $200/$300/$380, closes $311 (+68%), $5.55B raised, session cap ~$100B (~25× Series C for the interviewed investor). Supply: all on TSMC 5nm including a 750MW OpenAI commitment, but they skip HBM, CoWoS, and 3nm.

mental_model.name: Wafer-Scale × Skip the Three Bottlenecks × Decode Specialist
mental_model.components: Put compute, memory, and fabric on one wafer so you do not buy HBM/CoWoS/3nm. Survive a three-year stealth burn with national-lab proof. Let one huge customer (G42) create scale and political risk. In the agent era, sell tokens/second via API and split prefill/decode with hyperscalers who are not NVIDIA.
mental_model.application: Treat Cerebras as an inference-speed vendor, not a CUDA replacement. TSMC 5nm allocation is the hidden share-of-market. NVDA remains the default train/prefill stack Feldman will not partner. OpenAI 750MW is both demand and concentration risk.

key_insights.view: The hard problem was moving data, not FLOPs.
key_insights.question: Why a whole wafer?
key_insights.answer: HBM and multi-GPU hops dominate. 58× area and on-die SRAM make the transfer disappear — if you can hide ~46 defects with spare cores.

key_insights.view: G42 both made and nearly unmade the IPO.
key_insights.question: What did one customer change?
key_insights.answer: >$1B Condor Galaxy turned lab science into commercial scale and then into a listing delay. Concentration is the point.

key_insights.question: How do they live next to CUDA?
key_insights.answer: Split prefill (parallel, others' chips) and decode (serial, wafer). Sell 2000+ tok/s agents, not a training monopoly.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Wafer-scale inference speed plus hyperscaler decode split; IPO showed demand, TSMC 5nm and OpenAI 750MW are the constraints — medium
Only foundry that can make the wafer-scale part; even a CUDA rebel still buys 5nm — medium
